description: Cluster 1 (red):With 16 publications, cluster 1 is labeled ‘Transformation of customer experience in e-commerce through metaverse’. This cluster discusses how Metaverse has transformed customers’ e-commerce experience. Omnichannel, as a seamless shopping experience for customers across all channels, is part of the metaverse ecosystem. Hilken et al. (2018) depicted that augmented reality provides opportunities to ensure a smooth customer journey through embodied, embedded and extended experiences. Hoyer et al. (2020) brought forward the different stages of customers’ shopping journey (pre-, during and post-transaction) based on various technologies of Metaverse supported by artificial intelligence. Shankar et al. (2021) concluded that technology in retailing has transformed the ecosystem and faced unforeseen circumstances, not only by shoppers but also by retailers, employees and suppliers.

Cluster 2 (green):With 16 documents, cluster 2 labeled ‘Consumers interactivity in metaverse platform’. One of the main characteristics of a metaverse platform is its interactivity, providing engagement between buyer and seller. Yim, Chu, and Sauer (2017) discovered that augmented reality increases users’ web-based product interactivity through immersion based on usefulness and enjoyment in the metaverse condition. It contradicts the interactivity and immersion of conventional web conditions.Cowan and Ketron (2019) outline virtual reality product involvement to increase consumers’ interactivity to depict how they correspond to brands via virtual reality strategy. The approach enables consumers to respond by increasing telepresence, co-creation, and imagination. In another study, J. H. Kim et al. (2021) discovered a moderating effect of virtual reality experience among consumers between interactivity and perceived enjoyment and interactivity and perceived usefulness.

Cluster 3 (blue):This cluster is labeled ‘Theoretical adoption of metaverse technology’ and has seven publications. Metaverse technology is among the disruptive technologies requiring users to take time and be ready for adoption. These studies have adopted several theories to understand user adoption of metaverse technology using well-known theories in technology adoption. Rese et al. (2017) applied the technology acceptance model. They discovered that the hedonic domain (pleasure, enjoyment, fun) and utilitarian (information) vary in impact based on the different kinds of augmented reality applications. Saprikis et al. (2021) performed the unified theory on the acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) in adopting augmented reality technology in shopping malls. The finding shows that performance expectancy, reward, and enjoyment are the direct predictors of behavioural intention adoption, while others are indirect. Considering the outcome of technology adoption theory, Lee et al. (2020) discovered that the Delone and McLean Information System model was a crucial underlying theory in virtual reality as a marketing tool in the tourism and hospitality industry. It was found that system quality, content quality and vividness influence customers’ telepresence and attitude, subsequently leading to the intention to visit the destination. Table 6 summarizes the bibliographic coupling analysis with the three clusters in detail based on clusters, labels and representative publications.
